title: $j_!$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and let $j\colon U\to X$ be an open immersion of
the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})$ is bounded constructible
([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is the levelwise extension by zero
$D(j_!)K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek],
[sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]).

proof.text: The setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ and $U$ finite type over the field $k$. The field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, hence is Noetherian, and its one-point spectrum is quasi-compact. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure morphisms shows that $X$ and $U$ are Noetherian. In particular their underlying spaces are Noetherian, as also recalled explicitly for finite-type schemes over a field in [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Every subset of such a space is retrocompact. Since the whole space is quasi-compact, taking it as the quasi-compact open in the definition of retrocompactness shows that every subset is quasi-compact. In particular, the inverse image of every affine open under the absolute diagonal of either scheme is quasi-compact, so both $X$ and $U$ are quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Thus both schemes are qcqs, as required by the finite-stratification clause of constructibility. Consequently the open $U$ is retrocompact in $X$ and $j$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to the closed subset $X\setminus U$ to obtain its reduced induced closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. These facts verify the geometric hypotheses of the ringed open/closed lemma used below.

proof.text: The module functor $j_!$ is additive and exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Represent $K$ by a cochain complex $C$; the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] computes $D(j_!)K$ by the termwise complex $j_!C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to $j_!$ in each degree to obtain $H^q(D(j_!)K)\cong j_!H^q(K)$. Choose $a\leq b$ with $H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, as supplied by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. An additive functor sends a zero object to a zero object: the identity on its image is the image of the zero identity, hence zero. Therefore $H^q(D(j_!)K)=0$ for the same degrees; the cohomological bound is unchanged.

proof.text: Fix a constructible $\Lambda_U$-module $M$. By [sk-def-sfb-constructible], choose a finite constructible locally closed stratification $U=\coprod_a U_a$ such that each $M|_{U_a}$ has a finite constant local model over $\Lambda(*)$. By the definition of immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], each immersion $U_a\to U$ is closed in an open subscheme of $U$; that open subscheme is also open in $X$, so its composite $U_a\to X$ is an immersion. On underlying spaces, writing $U_a=V_a\cap F_a$ with $V_a$ open in $U$ and $F_a$ closed in $U$, choose a closed $C_a\subseteq X$ with $F_a=U\cap C_a$; then $U_a=V_a\cap C_a$ is locally closed in $X$. Along with $Z$ from step 1 these give a finite disjoint locally closed partition of $X$ in the sense of [def-constructible-stratification]. By the Noetherian clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset], all these subsets are constructible in $X$. Empty strata may be omitted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] with the arbitrary commutative ring sheaf $A=\Lambda_X$ and the complementary pair $(j,i)$ from step 1. The coefficient comparisons $g^{-1}\Lambda_X\simeq\Lambda_T$ for $g:T\to X$ are part of the restriction convention in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] defines the module pullback by transport followed by extension along this invertible comparison. Thus the ringed functors act on exactly our module categories. The $j_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] is the same ringed extension by zero: after identifying the source coefficient ring, both are left adjoint to the same restriction $R$. Explicitly, if these two left adjoints are $L,L\prime$, with units $\eta,\eta\prime$ and counits $\epsilon,\epsilon\prime$, their comparison at $M$ is $\epsilon_{L\prime M}\circ L(\eta\prime_M):LM\to L\prime M$, with inverse $\epsilon\prime_{LM}\circ L\prime(\eta_M)$. Write these maps as $c_M:LM\to L\prime M$ and $d_M:L\prime M\to LM$. Under the adjunction bijections, their definitions give $R(c_M)\circ\eta_M=\eta\prime_M$ and $R(d_M)\circ\eta\prime_M=\eta_M$. Therefore $R(d_M\circ c_M)\circ\eta_M=\eta_M$, so injectivity of the first adjunction bijection gives $d_M\circ c_M=\operatorname{id}_{LM}$. The second bijection gives $c_M\circ d_M=\operatorname{id}_{L\prime M}$ in the same way, since $R(c_M\circ d_M)\circ\eta\prime_M=\eta\prime_M$. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism of module objects. The quoted ringed lemma therefore gives $j^*j_!M\cong M$ and $i^*j_!M=0$ as module objects. If $s_a:U_a\to U$ denotes a stratum, the composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] gives $(j\circ s_a)^*j_!M\cong s_a^*j^*j_!M\cong s_a^*M$. Hence on $U_a$ the extension has the very same covers and scalar modules $P$ over $\Lambda(*)$ as $M$, not merely some finite presentation over the coefficient sheaf. On $Z$ its restriction is zero, which has the finite constant local model $\Lambda_Z\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}0$; the scalar module $0$ is finitely presented by the empty matrix. The partition in step 3 therefore witnesses constructibility of $j_!M$ according to [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

proof.text: For every $q$, the sheaf $M=H^q(K)$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Step 4 proves $j_!H^q(K)$ constructible, and the isomorphism in step 2 identifies it with $H^q(D(j_!)K)$. A local-model isomorphism remains a local-model isomorphism after composition with another isomorphism, so constructibility is invariant under this identification. Step 2 supplies the finite cohomological interval. These are precisely the two conditions of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and prove the claim. If $U$ or $Z$ is empty the corresponding family of nonempty strata is empty; the same zero model handles $K=0$ and the zero coefficient ring.
